Tagcast 0.60.0 brings the editor and player to their own desktop window, with
Electron apps for macOS, Windows and Linux. Python/source installations keep the
browser interface. Both routes share the same Tagcast server, interface and
iBroadcast integration.

## Tagcast on the desktop

- Standalone apps use **Electron 44.9.0**, with standard menus, zoom, fullscreen
  and system playback controls supported by Chromium and the operating system.
- Python and dependencies are bundled. No browser, Python or Node.js installation
  is needed for the desktop download. The browser CLI remains included.
- Closing the app stops only its own server, after accepted writes and read-back
  checks finish. A matching server already running is reused and left running.
- Existing account settings, sign-in tokens, cache and local album favourites
  remain in `~/.tagcast/`, or `TAGCAST_HOME`.
- Electron has its own Chromium profile. Browser-local preferences and Change
  history are separate from Safari/Chrome/Brave and are not copied automatically.
- Audio outputs still depend on the platform. Electron does not add native Sonos
  support or Safari's AirPlay picker; the shared Sound dialog retains volume,
  mute and the available output choices.

## Album favourites and ratings are independent

- The album heart now marks a **local, account-scoped favourite** without changing
  the album's stars. Changing stars never toggles the heart.
- Existing active five-star albums are imported once to preserve the earlier
  favourite list. Later ratings do not add favourites automatically.
- Album favourites are shared by Tagcast instances using the same local settings
  folder; they are not synced to iBroadcast or another computer.
- Track hearts retain their existing native iBroadcast rating behaviour.

## Quieter tracklists and mobile album pages

- Album tracklists omit repeated album-artist credits. A second line appears for
  distinct performers, composers, tags or a different stored file format.
- The common format is shown with the track summary. Different formats receive
  an amber label, so an MP3 among FLACs is easy to spot. No audio is downloaded
  to determine formats or quality.
- The playing track shows a speaker in place of its number and a subtle background.
  Actions appear on hover or keyboard focus; filled favourite hearts stay visible.
  Touch devices keep row actions visible.
- On mobile, the cover fills the available width above the title, artist, metadata
  and playback controls.

## Downloads and upgrading

- **macOS Apple Silicon:** `tagcast-0.60.0-macos-arm64.zip`.
- **macOS Intel:** `tagcast-0.60.0-macos-x64.zip`.
- **Windows x64:** `tagcast-0.60.0-windows-x64.zip`.
- **Linux x64:** `tagcast-0.60.0-linux-x64.tar.gz`.

Every archive has a separate SHA-256 file. Keep the complete extracted package
together. macOS apps have an ad-hoc integrity signature, without Developer ID
notarization; Windows downloads are not Authenticode signed. See the
[standalone guide](https://github.com/cyberdeliaAI/tagcast/blob/v0.60.0/docs/native-builds.md)
for opening instructions, the bundled CLI and platform requirements.

**Quit the older Tagcast before starting 0.60.0.** Electron rejects an older server
on its port rather than displaying the old application. Browser/source users can
continue with Python 3.11+, uv and the existing start scripts. The app does not
install updates automatically.

For Homebrew, quit Tagcast, then run `brew update` and
`brew upgrade --cask cyberdeliaAI/apps/tagcast` after the tap update is available.

All earlier editing, tags, reviewed cleanup, playlists and playback features stay
available. Tagcast never changes your local music files.
